inspiration: Armour as a timed reveal: unitarmor.frag keeps a sprite hidden except for moving horizontal bands whose spacing follows a sine wave of the sprite's height, and the progress value sets how much shows. Recreate: a build-in or armour-equip effect as a banded mask on the sprite, driven by one progress value.

Forcefield as an animated sparkle grid: shield.frag shifts the texture with a slow sine wobble, draws a diagonal sparkle pattern from modulo arithmetic on screen coordinates, and makes an edge glow by taking the maximum of four neighbour samples. Recreate: a shield or barrier shader with the same three parts (wobble, sparkle, edge) in our own pattern.

Modular unit sprites: sprite sources are split into base, leg, foot, joint-base, cell and heat-overlay files (for example atrax-leg, atrax-foot, anthicus-blade-heat, obviate-heat by name). Recreate: separate layers for walk parts and emissive heat, so one body can animate and glow without a new sheet.

Two separate planet images: serpulo and erekir are separate planet sprites (by file name), with planet and atmosphere vertex shaders (planet.vert, atmosphere.vert) and a star cubemap folder. Recreate: two world looks sharing one lighting and atmosphere rig; the palette contrast itself was not viewed.

Icon font mixed from many sources: one build config merges about 140 icons from several open icon sets with 53 custom glyphs. Recreate: one icon style guide and our own glyph set, rather than a patchwork.

Sound families by folder: ui, block, movement, explosions, beams, charge, shoot and loops, plus 16 music tracks named by role. Recreate: the same folder-by-role layout with our own audio, so the mixer can key on the folder.

Other animated surfaces exist as separate shaders by name (slag.frag, caustics.frag, fog.frag, mud.frag, cryofluid.frag); their contents were not read, so only the existence of a family of surface shaders is recorded here. A shared animated-surface shader with a palette input would be the natural recreation to check.

briefs.label: Legged siege walker (own label)
briefs.why: A multi-leg walker is easy to read at small size and animates well with separate leg and foot parts. Taken from file names (atrax-leg.png, atrax-foot.png, atrax.png); the art was not opened.
keep: separate leg and foot layers for a walk cycle
a silhouette that reads at small size (to confirm when viewed)
emissive heat layer on the body (see the heat overlay brief)
change: a different leg count and joint layout
our own palette and armour plates
a head design that is not the donor's

briefs.label: Hex-field barrier (own label)
briefs.why: A barrier that wobbles, sparkles and glows at its edge reads as a shield without any opaque art. Read from shield.frag.
change: triangle or rune-cell pattern instead of a plain grid
a different wave direction and speed

briefs.label: Banded build-in reveal (own label)
briefs.why: A unit that is revealed in moving bands during build or equip gives a clear progress cue. Read from unitarmor.frag.
keep: moving bands rather than a plain fade
change: diagonal or radial wipe instead of horizontal bands

briefs.label: Two-world planet pair (own label)
briefs.why: Two planet images with one contrasting palette each make the campaign read as two regions. Based on file names and shader names only.
keep: two planets with clearly different palettes
atmosphere ring as a separate pass
change: our own planet shapes and names

briefs.label: Emissive heat overlay (own label)
briefs.why: Glowing heat patches as a separate layer keep the base sprite cheap and let the glow pulse. Based on file names (anthicus-blade-heat.png, obviate-heat.png), not opened.
keep: emissive layer as its own sprite
change: patch shapes that follow our armour
